overview.title: Boats, Cafés and a Calmer Waterfront
overview.p1: Agadir’s marina is the polished waterfront alternative to the open beach: boats in the basin, café terraces, and a slower stroll for people who want sea air without sand in their shoes.
overview.p2: It works well for a coffee stop, an evening walk, or a seafood meal with a view of the masts. It is a contemporary resort design rather than an old historic harbour.
overview.p3: Combine it with the nearby beach or corniche. Forty-five to ninety minutes is enough unless you settle into a long restaurant terrace lunch.

q1.question: Is it free to walk around Agadir Marina?
q1.answer: Yes — public walkways are open; restaurants are à la carte.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit the Agadir Marina?
q2.answer: Late afternoon and evening are the most pleasant times when café terraces come alive.

q3.question: Are there restaurants at the marina?
q3.answer: Yes, the marina features seafood restaurants and cafés with water views.

q4.question: How far from the main beach?
q4.answer: It sits right at the northern end of the main beach promenade.

q5.question: Is Agadir Marina suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes, flat pedestrian walkways make it very accessible and safe for stroller strolls.
